Metadata.title: ToneProfile — From song to tone
Metadata.description: ToneProfile researches the rig, measures the recording and builds a preset for your guitar processor — starting with the Valeton GP-180 — and tells you exactly how sure it is.

Common.demoExplanation: This demo runs a simulated backend with fictional songs and invented sources. The interface, flow and data shapes are real; the analysis results are not.
Common.unknownError: Something went wrong on our side.
Common.networkError: We can't reach ToneProfile right now. Check your connection and try again.

descriptions.confirmed: Stated by the artist or a first-hand source about this recording.
descriptions.reported: Credible press about the artist's rig, not specific to this recording.
descriptions.likely: Several consistent sources, or strong evidence in the audio.
descriptions.inferred: Reasoned from style, era or the audio — not stated by any source.
descriptions.unknown: We couldn't find out. We won't guess.

specificity.artist_general: About the artist's rig in general

hero.title: From song to tone.
hero.lede: Pick a song. ToneProfile researches the rig, measures the recording and builds a preset for your guitar processor — then shows you exactly how sure it is.
hero.illustration: Illustration of the analysis pipeline with a fictional song.
hero.outcomeTitle: Tone profile ready · GP-180 preset built
hero.outcomeBody: Clean and bright, with a dotted-eighth delay and wide ambience — six modules, every value explained.
hero.outcomeSignature: Tone signature of the illustrated tone: clean, bright, strong ambience.

how.title: Four layers between a record and your pedal.

reference.title: Reference
reference.body: A song, and optionally a short excerpt you upload. We never download music for you.

evidence.title: Evidence
evidence.body: What the artist is documented to have used — with sources — plus what we measure in the audio.

intent.title: Tone profile
intent.body: A device-independent description: signal chain, amp character, gain, EQ balance, ambience.

device.title: Your device
device.body: A deterministic engine translates the profile into real models and knob values for your processor.

evidence.title: Every claim shows its confidence and its source.
evidence.body: AI tools love to sound certain. ToneProfile separates what is documented, what is measured and what is inferred — and says “unknown” when that's the honest answer.

translation.title: One tone. Rebuilt with the models your device actually has.
translation.body: Knob positions don't transfer between amps. So we don't copy numbers — we map each block of the tone profile to the closest model on your device and solve its settings.

device.title: Valeton GP-180, done properly.
device.body: A downloadable preset for Valeton Suite, a printable dial-in sheet and import instructions. More processors will follow the same tone profile — when we can do them properly too.

points.file: Preset file you import with Valeton Suite
points.sheet: Dial-in sheet for every block and knob
points.versions: Versions you can compare and rate

limits.title: A preset is a starting point, not a time machine.

items.hands: Your hands, guitar and strings are part of the tone. We ask about your pickups and compensate — we can't replace practice.
items.studio: Records are mixed, doubled and mastered. We describe the guitar sound, not the studio.
items.uncertain: Some rigs are simply undocumented. When that happens we tell you, and lean on what we can measure.

Profile.title: Tone profile
Profile.lede: What we found, independent of any device.

fingerprint.title: Tone fingerprint
fingerprint.description: Average spectrum of the guitar in the excerpt, loudness-normalized. Select a band to see what it means.
fingerprint.noAudio: No excerpt was analysed, so there's no measured spectrum. Upload an excerpt next time for a measured fingerprint.
fingerprint.chartLabel: Spectrum chart. Use the band buttons below it for details.

bandInfo.body: Low end and thump. Too much sounds boomy, too little sounds thin.
bandInfo.warmth: Where a tone gets thick or muddy. Often cut in dense mixes.
bandInfo.mids: The core of a guitar in a band mix — where it sits against vocals.
bandInfo.bite: Pick attack and cut. Most tones that “cut through” push here.
bandInfo.air: Sparkle on clean tones, fizz on distorted ones. Cabs and mics shape this.

targets.title: Tone character
targets.lede: Perceptual targets the device engine solves for.

chain.title: Signal chain
chain.lede: Device-independent: each block is a role and an archetype.

evidence.title: Evidence
evidence.lede: Gear claims found by research. Claims whose quotes couldn't be verified in their source were removed.
evidence.empty: No documented gear for this song. The profile relies on the audio and inference.

signature.title: Tone signature
signature.lede: The measured spectrum wrapped into a circle, surrounded by the tone's character. Two tones that sound different look different.
signature.ledeNoAudio: The tone's character around the circle. No excerpt was measured, so there's no spectrum at the centre.
signature.aria: Tone signature: {summary}. The same values are listed under Tone character.
signature.hint: Select a characteristic to see it in the signature, the fingerprint and the signal chain.

Preset.lede: The tone profile, rebuilt with the models your device has.
Preset.noAlternatives: No close alternatives on this device.

checks.catalog_models: Models exist on this device and firmware
checks.chain_order: Chain order accepted by the device

unavailable.demo_mode: Preset files are produced by the ToneProfile engine and aren't available in the demo. The dial-in sheet has every setting.
unavailable.validation_failed: This version failed validation, so we won't give you a file for it.
unavailable.format_unverified: File export for this device is still being verified on hardware. Use the dial-in sheet for now.

sheet.title: Dial-in sheet
sheet.lede: Every enabled block and knob, in signal order. Set these by hand on the device or in Valeton Suite.

steps.connect: Connect the GP-180 to your computer with USB and open Valeton Suite.
steps.slot: Pick an empty user patch slot so you don't overwrite a preset you care about.
steps.import: Use the patch import function in Valeton Suite and choose the downloaded .prst file.
steps.level: Play at a moderate volume first and adjust the patch volume to match your other presets.
steps.compare: If a value looks different on the device, trust the dial-in sheet and tell us in the feedback.

Feedback.title: How close did it get?
Feedback.lede: Try it on your device first. Your rating trains the engine's priorities, not your data.
